summary: Correct, general fix for duplicate options from joined limit_choices_to: replaces complex_filter join with a correlated Exists(OuterRef('pk')) subquery using _base_manager, which is the standard Django approach to dedupe. No correctness, regression, or compatibility problems block merge.

issues.description: Guard changed from `if limit_choices_to is not None:` to `if limit_choices_to:`, so empty dict `{}` / empty `Q()` now skip filtering instead of applying a no-op filter. Behaviorally equivalent (empty filter was a no-op) but a subtle semantic shift worth noting.

Swaps a join-based filter for an Exists() correlated subquery; generally fine and the correct way to dedupe, but on some backends/queries the subquery form can have different performance characteristics than the prior join.
